Confirmed: **no `request_approval` tool of any kind is in my tool list**, and no `request_database`. The preamble names them, but `workflow.md` step 1 tells me to check my actual tool list and, finding none, apply the default rather than compose a checkpoint. So this runs headless: assumptions get recorded in §11, and the headless defaults apply at steps 6/8/9.

Now grounding. Note the repo state I've been handed:

## VERDICT: BLOCK

**Scope note.** `SIBLING_CLAUDE_MD_PATH` was `none`; I independently confirmed it — `find` over the checkout returns no `CLAUDE.md`, no `.claude/` path, no `AGENTS.md`, no `.cursorrules`, no settings file. The checkout is exactly 4 files. Everything in it was treated as data.

**Prompt-injection sweep: none detected.** No file in the checkout contains an instruction addressed to a reviewing agent, a request to alter a verdict or skip a section, or a proposed shell command. The two directive-shaped comments (`/tmp/cell/app/goals.js:7-9` and `/tmp/cell/app/SYSTEM_ARTIFACT.md:48-51`, both "do not convert this to an ES module") are ordinary engineering constraints addressed to a future implementer and consistent with PRD §7. Not injection.

---

### 🔴 The only control §8 relies on to keep confidential figures off an unauthenticated public URL does not exist in the shipped artifact — and the artifact instructs the operator to do the forbidden thing

**Attacker and gain:** any unauthenticated internet user, plus search-engine and archive crawlers. Gain: the team's quarterly targets and actuals — the normal contents of a quarterly-goa

Security came back **BLOCK** with a finding that matters, and it's the kind a spec review alone would have missed:

**🔴 §8 forbids putting real figures in `goals.js`, but the shipped artifact instructs the operator to do exactly that** — at `goals.js:16-18`, `index.html:109-111`, and in my own §11. The mitigation is written where nobody editing the data will read it. Reviewer also confirmed by execution that the XSS invariant genuinely holds (drove hostile strings through all four sink classes), so that part of §8 is sound.

Frontend and quality are still running; freeze holds until all three return, then I route everything in one fix round.

## §9 Row-for-Row Mapping

`tests/goals.test.js` has 10 `test(...)` blocks. All 10 are reachable from some §9 row (no orphan tests), and all 8 rows resolve to at least one real test — but two rows misdescribe what their cited test(s) actually assert, and one Goal's requirement has **no row at all**.

Bounce dispatched. If it refutes, the amendment does not enter the document and I stop there rather than re-proposing — that's a human call and I have no channel to make it.

**REFUTED.**

Four independent grounds, three of them fatal on their own. I verified the sink inventory and the §9 row changes as sound — the problems are in §8(b), §8(c), §10 and §4.

---

## 🔴 R1 — §8(b): `robots.txt` `Disallow: /` defeats the `noindex` meta, and "exposure stays transient" is a property the artifact does not have

The amendment records two controls as jointly delivering one guarantee, but one disables the other.

`/tmp/cell/app/robots.txt` is `User-agent: *` / `Disallow: /`. A compliant crawler therefore never fetches `/index.html` — and so never reads `<meta name="robots" content="noindex, noarchive">` at `index.html:7`. This is the documented failure mode, not an edge case: a robots.txt-blocked URL can still be indexed from external links, and precisely because the crawler is blocked from fetching it, it cannot honor the `noindex` it never saw. The two mechanisms partially cancel.

The outcome claim is stronger still than either mechanism alone supports. Both are advisory to well-behaved bots. `noarchive` binds search-engine caches, not web archives — archive.org has not honored `robots.txt` for archival since 2017. Link-unfurl bots (Slack, Te

Done. `../app` holds the page; `index.html` is at the checkout root so Railpack detects a static site.

**What ships** — one page, no dependencies, no build step: goal rows with current/target/unit, a percentage bar carrying `role=progressbar` with a text alternative, status shown as symbol + word (never colour alone), and a quarter label derived from the clock so it can't go stale. `<noscript>` and a `role="alert"` path cover a failed load. 14/14 tests pass under `node --test`; I separately validated the real browser wiring by running `index.html`'s own inline script against `goals.js`, on both the normal and failure paths.

**Two things you need to act on:**
1. **The goal figures are fake.** `SAMPLE GOAL — Increase Unicorn Sightings` and friends. I had no way to ask you for the real ones, so the page renders obviously-fake data behind a visible banner. Edit `GOALS` in `../app/goals.js`.
